cause.proximate_text: The cause of the event was inadequate venting of the intercooler coolant system during maintenance. Venting was performed during the start of one of the initial PMT runs and not performed when the engine was hot.

nodes.proximate_text: The cause of the event was inadequate venting of the intercooler coolant system during maintenance. Venting was performed during the start of one of the initial PMT runs and not performed when the engine was hot.

nodes.display_name: Air introduced into intercooler coolant system during maintenance
nodes.description: Air entered the intercooler coolant and jacket water systems when they were drained and refilled for planned maintenance beginning 1/26/20.
Venting was performed during an initial PMT run rather than when the engine was hot/loaded, failing to remove entrained air; vendor later recommended venting be done when hot and loaded.

nodes.display_name: Residual air remained in coolant system undetected
nodes.description: Post-maintenance testing did not identify the retained air condition prior to returning the diesel generator to operable status on 2/7/20.

nodes.display_name: Coolant pump unable to establish normal system pressure
nodes.description: Air in the intercooler coolant system prevented the pump from establishing normal system pressure during the 2/26/20 surveillance start.

nodes.display_name: E-1 tripped on low intercooler coolant pressure
nodes.description: Engine automatically tripped at approximately 2129 on 2/26/20 due to low intercooler coolant pressure after reaching full speed.

nodes.display_name: E-1 Emergency Diesel Generator inoperable / TS 3.8.1 not complied with
Vent intercooler coolant system and return E-1 to operable
Revise procedures to require venting when engine is hot and loaded

notes: No official cause code was assigned in block 13/block 18 data provided (block_13 empty, cause_code TBD); cause node marked provisional per rule 4. No backup EDGs modeled as BACKED_UP_BY because the narrative describes E-2/E-3/E-4 surveillance tests as separate, unrelated activities, not as backups actively covering E-1's inoperability window in a stated-operable capacity for this failure chain (they were each briefly inoperable themselves during their own tests) -- TS analysis on multiple-DG-inoperable overlap is noted in Analysis but does not describe a backup relationship to the E-1 failure chain itself, so omitted per rule 6 ambiguity guidance really it's DESIGN CONTEXT / redundancy discussion, not a backup edge target for the E-1 consequence node.
